Neutral

/NOO-trul/ — rhymes with central · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Someone or something that is neutral does not take sides or favor any one position in a disagreement or conflict.

A referee must remain neutral, favoring neither team.

Worked Example

When her two best friends had a terrible falling out, Jasmine listened to both of them but refused to side with either, even though each girl begged her to take her side.

Neutral is more precise than 'quiet' or 'undecided' because it describes an active choice not to favor either side in a conflict, especially when pressure to choose exists. It's about maintaining balance in a dispute.

How Neutral Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

objective

objective: sticking to facts, not personal opinions

disinterested

disinterested: having no personal stake in the outcome

unbiased

unbiased: not leaning toward either side

Antonyms

partisan

partisan: strongly devoted to one side or party

allied

allied: joined to one side as a supporter

How Strong Is It? — biased → opinionated → uncommitted → neutral

biased vs. neutral

biased vs. neutral: Biased is the far opposite of neutral: a biased observer leans strongly toward one side, while a neutral one has no stake in either.

opinionated vs. neutral

opinionated vs. neutral: Opinionated is still far from neutral — an opinionated person pushes strong views on everything, whereas a neutral person declines to take a side at all.

uncommitted vs. neutral

uncommitted vs. neutral: Uncommitted comes close to neutral but is weaker: an uncommitted person simply has not chosen a side yet, while a truly neutral person deliberately stands outside the conflict entirely.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — neutr-

Root — neutr-: neither of two (Latin (neuter, from ne- 'not' + uter 'which of two'))

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: relating to (Latin (-alis))

Put it together

Put it together: Put neutr- ('neither of two') together with -al ('relating to') and you get 'belonging to neither side' — exactly what a neutral referee or country is: not involved with, and not favoring, either party in a conflict.

Use the root in a new word: neutralize

Use the root in a new word: neutralize: In science class the base neutralized the acid, canceling both out so the solution was neither acidic nor basic — the 'neither' root of neutral in action.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral to formal

Use neutral when someone must choose not to take a side in a conflict or disagreement and succeeds in remaining fair to both. For general objectivity without a conflict, 'objective' or 'unbiased' may be more precise. Neutral is strongest when applied to conflicts where choosing a side is tempting or expected.
